stem: When it is noon along 820 30' E longitude along what degree of longitude it will be 6.30 a.m.?
expl: When there is a midday at 82030' E longitude then 6:30 in the morning means there is a difference of 5:30 hrs in time. As in one hour the change in longitude is 150 therefore 820 30' difference in 5:30 hours is 820 30' – 820 30' = 00 latitude.

stem: If the difference of longitudes for the two places is 900, the time interval between these places will be –
expl: Generally, 10 longitude is equal to a difference of 4 minutes. 900 longitude means 90 × 4 = 360 minutes or 6 hours. Hence (b) is the correct answer.

stem: When, there is mid-day in the Greenwich, local time of a place is 5 O'clock evening. At which of the following longitude (meridians) that place will be located –
expl: According to the question, when it is mid-day at Greenwich there is 5 O'clock somewhere in the evening. This means the time of that place is ahead of Greenwich time. Hence, that place is located to the east of Greenwich. The Difference in time is 5 hours. Therefore, 1 hour = 60 minutes 5 hours = 5 × 60 = 300 minutes As this place is located to the east of the Greenwich line hence this place is located at 750 E.

stem: Which one of the following longitudes along with the Prime Meridian forms a great circle on the globe.
expl: The Prime Meridian is the zero degree line of longitude that passes near London. The Prime Meridian was accepted as Zero degrees longitude at an international conference in 1884. It is also known as the Greenwich meridian. Just opposite to 0o longitude there is an imaginary line located at about 1800 E or W as the International Date Line which forms a great circle with the Prime Meridian along the globe.

Katchal is situated nearly 1600 km away from the mainland of India and at a distance of 418 km from Port Blair Port and between the 7056' North latitude and 930 24' East Meridian. Therefore, the nearest option will be (d).

stem: The basis of deciding the standard time of any place is–
expl: Prime Meridian line is also known as the International Meridian or Greenwich Meridian. This line passes through England’s Royal Greenwich Observatory. Line situated at zero degrees longitude determines the International Standard Time. 1800 longitude is called the International Date Line. The Prime Meridian (00 longitude) passes through the following countries – (1) United Kingdom, (2) France, (3) Spain, (4) Algeria, (5) Mali, (6) Burkina-Faso, (7) Togo, (8) Ghana.

stem: Which one of the following cities does not have the same clock time as that of the other three Cities at any given instant?
expl: London (U.K.), Lisbon (Portugal) and Accra (Ghana) have similar time as all three use Greenwich time. Addis Ababa the capital of Ethiopia is located at 380 45' E, whose time is 2 hours, 35 minutes, ahead of GMT. Note - The Standard time of Ethiopia is 3 hours ahead of Greenwich time. So, Addis Ababa is the correct answer.

stem:
The standard time of the following countries is ahead of or behind Greenwich Mean Time depending on whether they are East or West of the longitude passing through Greenwich.
(1) Cuba (2) Greece
(3) Iraq (4) Costa Rica
(5) Japan
Which one of the following sequential orders gives the correct arrangement of the countries according to their standard time from ahead to behind GMT?
expl: Greenwich line (0o longitude) passes through England. World standard time is measured from here. Time in Eastern Hemisphere is ahead of the Western Hemisphere. The standard time of the above mentioned countries is given below : Japan = +9 hours Iraq = + 3 hours Greece = + 2 hours Cuba = –5 hours Costa Rica = –6 hours Hence, the correct sequence of standard time ahead to behind GMT is 5, 3, 2, 1, 4 Japan, Iraq, Greece, Cuba and Costa Rica.

stem: When there is noon at I.S.T. meridian people another place of the Earth is taking their 6 O'clock morning tea. The longitude of the place is :
expl: The Earth makes one rotation (3600) in 24 hours, which means it passes through 150 in an hour from West to East. Every 150 we go Westward, local time becomes 1 hour behind the place, given in the question, which is 6:00 hours behind the I.S.T. (82030'E). So it is situated to the west of the I.S.T. 6:00 hour difference is equal to 900 longitudes (15×6 = 90). Thus, the place is situated at 900 west with respect to I.S.T. This gives the longitude of the place (with respect to Greenwich) as 7030' W (820.30' E-900=7030'W).

stem: A telegram was sent from Greenwich at 12.00 Noon. The time for transmission was 12 minutes. It reached a town at 6.00 p.m. The longitude of the town will be :
expl: Earth rotates on its axis in 24 hours and therefore completes the angle of 3600 in one rotation (i.e. 150 in an hour or 10 in 4 minutes). As the telegram sent from Greenwich at 12:00 noon reached another city at 6:00 evening and 12 minutes passed in messaging the telegram. The, total time = 6 hours – 12 minutes = 360 minutes – 12 minutes = 348 minutes. As we know for 60 minutes = 150 longitude for 348 minutes = 15 × 348/600 = 870 This is now clear that place where the telegram reached at 6:00 evening will be at 870 East longitude.

stem: International Date Line passes through –
expl: International Date Line is an imaginary line on the Earth that separates two consecutive days on the calendar. This line passes through 1800 opposite to Greenwich (England) from the Pacific Ocean. This line turns when any land area falls in the way of this line.

stem: There is no minimum distance between two places on the globe :
expl: Except for the International Date Line (1800 meridian), meridians at all other places follow the same path. The International Date Line has been turned at 8 places on the globe so that disputes about the date at the same place not occur. As the International Date Line has been turned on its way near the Alaska, therefore the minimum distance between two places on the globe at the International Date Line cannot exist.

stem: If the earth's direction of rotation is reversed, what should be the IST when it is noon at the International Date Line?
expl: Time difference between International Date Line (IDL) and GMT is of 12 hours. Noon (12 pm) at IDL means midnight (12 am) at GMT. I.S.T. is GMT + 5:30 hours, but, in the question 'the Earth's direction of rotation is reversed'. So that I.S.T. becomes GMT-5:30 hours. In this way, it should be 6:30 pm at I.S.T. (instead of 5:30am).

stem: Which one of the following Straits is nearest to the International Date Line?
expl: The Prime Meridian line or the Greenwich line is situated at 00 Meridian and on the 1800 East or West side of it lies the International Date Line So either from the East or from the West side of this line the place at the nearest meridian will be nearest to the Date Line. The meridian of straits given in the options is as follows – Malacca - 990 32' East Meridian Bering Strait - 1680 23'West Meridian Strait of Florida - 820 23' West Meridian Strait of Gibraltar - 50 41' West Meridian From the above data, it is clear that Bering Strait (1680 23' West Meridian) is the closest place to the International Date Line.

stem: A ship is moving from the eastern side of Aleutian Islands towards Dutch Harbour. It crosses 1800 meridian on 1st January 1999 at 23:30 hr. What time and date will be recorded by the captain of the ship in his diary after one-hour journey from the point of crossing of the meridian?
expl: Aleutian Island’s eastern end lies at the west of 1800 Meridian, (1720 East longitude) while Dutch Harbour lies at the east side of 1800 Meridian i.e at (1660 31' 55" West longitude). As the movement of the ship from West to East of the 1800 Meridian, the date will lag behind by 1 day. So, at 23:30 hr. 1 January 1999 crossing 180 Meridian by rule the date should be 31 December 1998 and after 1 hour (23.30 + 60 = 2400 + 30) captain of the ship will record 00:30 hr. 1 January, 1999. But actually, the International Date Line does not completely follow the 180 Meridian to avoid segregating the places with equal political and economic entities (including Aleutian Islands and Dutch Harbor). In the context of this situation International Date Line is not crossed by the ship and the day will be same even after 1 hour the captain of the ship will record 00:30 hr. on 2 January, 1999.

stem: Captain of a ship moving Westward records the local time of 10-00 hrs Monday at 90o W. If the speed of the ship is the same as the speed of the rotation of the earth, which of the following local time and day would be found by the captain at International date line:
expl: Captain of the ship traveling westward recorded the local time 10:00 hours at 900 west Meridian, this means that the ship is near the North American continent. Since the Earth rotates from west to east on its axis (anticlockwise) and the ship is moving towards west with the speed equivalent to the Earth’s rotation therefore, both are moving in opposite directions but there is no effect of Earth’s rotation upon the movement of objects upon its surface. So, for the ship covering 900 meridian it requires the time of 6 hours and the ship will be behind 6 hours according to local time. Therefore, when reaching the International Date Line he will write the local time as the same 10:00 hrs Monday. However, when he crosses the International Date Line his local time will be 10:00 hours Tuesday.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Anadyr in Siberia and Nome in Alska are a few kilometers from each other, but when people are waking up and getting set for breakfast in these cities, it would be different days.
II. When it is Monday in Anadyr, it is Tuesday in Nome
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: Anadyr and Nome are relatively close to each other about 800 km apart and because of the International Date Line and a time difference of about 20–21 hours, their breakfast times fall on different calendar days. That is, when people in Anadyr are having breakfast on Monday morning, at the same moment it is late Sunday morning in Nome the days are different (Monday at one place, Sunday at the other). Anadyr’s date is either the same as Nome’s date or one day ahead of it. No matter how you calculate, a situation cannot arise in which it is Monday in Anadyr and Tuesday in Nome; because of their geographical position and the IDL, Nome is always either on the same date as Anadyr or behind it never ahead. Thus, only Statement I is correct.

stem: Which path must be followed by a Ship to move from one place to another in the least time ?
expl: For a ship to travel in the least possible time from one place to another, it must travel with respect to the Meridian. At the 1800 meridian traveling from east to west, it gets one day less in this way while moving from west to east one day increases.

stem: The local time of a place is 6:00 AM when the Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) is 3:00 AM, what is the longitude of the place ?
expl: Greenwich Mean Time (G.M.T.) is referred to as Coordinated Universal Time (U.T.C.). International time is calculated from Greenwich at the 0 Meridian, and the time eastward of it is while the time westward of it is behind (although dates are measured from the 1800 meridian at the International Date Line which passes through the mid of the Pacific Ocean). Meridians situated 1800 east of Greenwich are called East-meridians and meridians situated at 1800 west are known as West-meridians. All the meridians in 3600 of the globe are divided into 24 time zones (150 – 150 meridian difference). Therefore, each time zone has a 1 hour time difference and each meridian has the difference of 4 minutes, moving each meridian east G.M.T. time is 4 minutes ahead and moving west of G.M.T. time remains 4 minutes behind for each meridian. According to the question time is to be calculated for that place which is ahead (6-3=3 hrs) of Greenwich. As we know for 1 hours difference in longitude (meridian) is 150 therefore for 3 hours the difference will be 15 × 3 = 450 , So that place will lie at 450 east of Greenwich.

stem: What is the local time of Thimphu (Bhutan) located at 900 East longitude when the time at Greenwich (00) is 12:00 noon :
expl: Difference between Greenwich and Thimphu (Bhutan) Total time difference = 90 × 4 = 360 minutes ∴ The time increases at a rate of 4 minutes per one degree of longitude. = 6 hours / Local time of Thimphu is 6 hours more than that at Greenwich i.e. 6.00 p.m.

stem: Which one of the following is not a natural unit of time?
expl: According to the question, the standard time has been arti-ficially determined from the given alternatives. For example, the 00 longitude line has been determined as the prime meridian. Similarly, the 82 East longitude line has been set as the standard time of India, while the tropical year, the lunar month and the day are the natural units of time.

stem:
Consider the following countries :
I. United Kingdom II. Denmark
III. New Zealand IV. Australia
V. Brazil How many of the above countries have more than four time zones?
expl: The United Kingdom has more than 4 (a total of 9) time zones. Mainland Denmark has only one time zone, but when the entire Danish Realm is included—covering autonomous territories such as Greenland and the Faroe Islands : the total number of time zones becomes six. On the basis of widely accepted international data, New Zealand and its associated states/areas together have 5 time zones. Australia, along with its dependent territories, has a total of 9 time zones. Brazil has a total of four time zones. Therefore, when the total number of time zones is calculated for each “country” by including its dependencies/overseas territories as well, the number of countries in the given list that have more than four time zones is four.
